title: The Wrong Train to Kyoto: How Travel Quietly Rewires Your Thinking
title_zh: 开往京都的那趟错车：旅行如何悄悄改写你的思维
intro_zh: 本文约 522 词，共 8 段，重点讲旅行如何通过陌生感、视角、适应、邂逅与反差改变人的思维方式；含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（unfamiliar, perspective, adapt, curiosity, encounter, contrast），句子难度中等，配 4 道阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: Most people bring home hundreds of photos from a trip and almost nothing else. Yet the changes that really matter are rarely in the album. They hide in the way a traveler reads a menu, waits in a queue, or talks to a stranger six months later. Travel is not only a place you go to; it is also a habit of noticing that you carry back with you.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数人旅行归来，带回家的只有几百张照片，别的几乎没有。然而真正重要的改变很少留在相册里。它们藏在旅行者六个月后看菜单、排队等候、或与陌生人交谈的方式中。旅行不只是你去过的一个地方，它还是你带回来的一种留心观察的习惯。

paragraphs.en: Travel works on the mind because it makes ordinary things strange. In a foreign supermarket, even buying milk becomes a small puzzle: which size, which brand, whether to weigh the fruit yourself. The brain, forced to notice details it normally ignores, wakes up. Psychologists describe this mild discomfort as useful stress — the kind that pushes people to learn faster and remember more of what they learn.
paragraphs.zh: 旅行之所以作用于头脑，是因为它让寻常事物变得陌生。在国外的超市里，连买牛奶都成了一个小谜题：买多大包装、选哪个牌子、水果是否要自己称重。大脑被迫去注意平时忽略的细节，于是被唤醒了。心理学家把这种轻微的不适称为“有用的压力”——正是它促使人们学得更快，也记得更牢。

paragraphs.en: The second gift is perspective. A student from Shanghai who spends a month in a small Italian town notices that shops close at one in the afternoon, that dinner begins at eight, and that nobody apologizes for either. Slowly she understands something simple but powerful: her own timetable is a choice, not a law of nature. Whole ways of living, which felt fixed, turn out to be one option among many.
paragraphs.zh: 第二份礼物是视角。一位上海学生在意大利小镇住了一个月，她注意到商店下午一点就关门，晚饭八点才开始，而且没有人为此道歉。慢慢地，她明白了一件简单却有力的事：自己的时间表是一种选择，而非自然规律。那些原以为固定不变的生活方式，原来只是众多选项中的一个。

paragraphs.en: Research supports the idea. In a 2019 survey of 1,500 university students, those who had lived abroad for at least four weeks scored about 8 percent higher on tests of flexible thinking than those who had stayed home. The gain was not huge, but it lasted for months after the trip ended — long after the souvenirs had been put away on a shelf.
paragraphs.zh: 研究支持这一看法。2019 年一项针对 1500 名大学生的调查显示，那些在国外生活过至少四周的学生，在灵活思维测试中的得分比待在家里的学生高出约 8%。这一提升并不巨大，却在旅行结束数月之后依然存在——那时纪念品早已被收上架子。

paragraphs.en: The third change appears when things go wrong. A missed train, a lost key, a dish far hotter than expected: travel hands you small problems and takes away your familiar tools. To adapt, travelers learn to ask again, to wait without anger, and to laugh at their own mistakes. Here curiosity matters more than confidence. People who accept that they will look foolish for a week often learn the most.
paragraphs.zh: 第三种改变出现在事情出错的时候。误了火车、丢了钥匙、菜辣得远超预期：旅行把小麻烦塞给你，又把熟悉的工具拿走。为了适应，旅行者学会再去问一次、不带火气地等待、并对自己的错误一笑置之。此时好奇心比自信更重要。那些愿意接受“自己会笨拙一周”的人，往往收获最多。

paragraphs.en: Encounters with strangers do much of the work. A sixty-year-old shopkeeper in Lisbon explains, in three languages and a great deal of hand-waving, how to find the right bus. Ten minutes later you are on it, and the city feels less like a map and more like a place where people live. Such moments teach a lesson no lecture can: most people are helpful, and a misunderstanding is usually harmless.
paragraphs.zh: 与陌生人的偶遇起了很大作用。里斯本一位六十岁的店主用三种语言加上大量手势，向你解释怎样才能找到对的公交车。十分钟后你已经坐在车上，这座城市不再像一张地图，而更像一个有人生活的地方。这样的时刻教给人课堂讲不出的道理：多数人是乐于助人的，而误会通常无害。

paragraphs.en: Then comes contrast. Coming home is part of the trip. The street you have walked down for ten years suddenly looks different — the noise, the food, the way people stand in line. Travel does not make your home worse; it makes it visible. You begin to see which habits you keep because you chose them and which ones you simply inherited.
paragraphs.zh: 接着出现的是反差。回家也是旅行的一部分。你走了十年的那条街忽然看起来不一样了——噪音、食物、人们排队的样子。旅行不会让你的家乡变差，而是让它变得清晰可见。你开始分辨：哪些习惯是你自己选择的，哪些只是从上一辈继承下来的。

paragraphs.en: You do not need a passport to start. Take a bus to the end of the line, eat where the menu has no pictures, ask one stranger a question and really listen to the answer. Travel broadens the mind only when attention travels with the body — and that journey can begin three stops from home.
paragraphs.zh: 你并不需要护照才能开始。坐一趟车到终点站，去菜单上没有图片的小店吃饭，向一个陌生人提个问题并认真听完答案。只有注意力随身体一同出发，旅行才会真正开阔眼界——而这段旅程，可以从离你家三站路的地方开始。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Travel is mainly about taking good photographs.
People should live abroad for at least a month.
Travel changes people most by changing how they notice and think.
Foreign supermarkets are too confusing for tourists.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从陌生感、视角、适应、偶遇、反差等角度说明旅行真正改变的是人的观察方式与思维方式，而不是照片或地点，故答案为 C。

questions.q: According to the 2019 survey mentioned in the passage, what was true of students who had lived abroad for at least four weeks?
options: They spent much more money on souvenirs.
They forgot their own habits very quickly.
They preferred to stay at home afterwards.
They scored about 8 percent higher on tests of flexible thinking.
questions.explain: 细节题。第四段明确提到，在国外生活至少四周的学生在灵活思维测试中得分高出约 8%，故选 D。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the Shanghai student who stayed in a small Italian town?
options: She decided to move to Italy permanently.
She found Italian food too hot for her.
She came to see her own daily timetable as one choice among many.
She believed shops should stay open all afternoon.
questions.explain: 推断题。第三段说她意识到自己的作息是一种选择而非自然规律，说明她把自己的生活方式看作众多选项之一，故选 C；其余选项文中均无依据。

questions.q: The word adapt in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: 词义题。该段讲旅行中遇到误车、丢钥匙等小麻烦时，旅行者学会再问一次、耐心等待，即“适应新情况、作出调整”，故选 B。
